_comment: S2273 - the watch screen shapes the app is verified on, as data rather than as a remembered
AVD name. Play's Wear quality criterion WO-V16 ('Watch shapes') requires content to fit the
physical display, to overlap nothing, to be cut off by no edge, and to work on a circle no
smaller than 192 dp. The guideline names the two emulators a reviewer uses, and both carry
Why this file exists: until 2026-09-02 the project owned exactly one watch AVD, Wear_OS_XL_Round
at 240 dp - larger than BOTH reviewer devices - and nothing in the repository recorded that. The
app was rejected on 2026-08-31 for a defect that is invisible at 240 dp and blocks first launch
at 192 dp. A bench nobody can check is a bench nobody notices is wrong.
contentBoxDp is what wearScreenInsets() leaves for content: the round inset takes 0.10 of the
shorter edge on each side, so the usable box is 0.8 of the diameter. Size a fixed-width row
against the SMALLEST reviewed value, not against the device on the desk. A row wider than that
cannot fit at any scroll position, because scrolling moves content vertically.
densityDpi is the AVD's hw.lcd.density; dp = widthPx / densityDpi * 160.
Consumed by scripts/devtest/wear-shape-bench.ps1 and the watch pre-release sweep.

profiles.note: The floor WO-V16 names. Smallest content box, so every fixed-width row is sized against this one.
The owner's physical watch is close to this size, which is why measurements taken on it read as safe.
Not a reviewer device. Kept as the regression control: a fix for 192 dp must not break this one.
